items.text: KEY POINT KEYPOINT

items.label: text
items.text: 1 mol of Zn reacts with 1 mol of CuSO, therefore 0.0100 mol of CuSO reacts with 0.0100 mol of Zn. We added 0.0185 mol of Zn, so Zn is in excess. 1 mol of Zn reacts with 1 mol of CuSO4, therefore 0.0100 mol of CuSO reacts with 0.0100 mol of Zn. We added 0.0185 mol of Zn, so Zn is in excess.

items.text: REMINDER REMINDER

items.text: Remember that we have to divide the volume by 1000 to convert it to dm³ because the concentration is given in mol/dm³. Remember that we have to divide the volume by 1000 to convert it to dm³ because the concentration is given in mol/dm³.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXTENSION WORK

items.label: text
items.text: You could repeat this experiment with metals of different reactivities. The more reactive a metal is, the more heat should be released in the displacement reaction. Make sure you keep everything else the same: the number of moles of the metals, the size of the solid particles, and the volume and concentration of the copper(ll) sulfate solution. Do not use metals that are more reactive than magnesium, otherwise you are measuring the heat released when the metal reacts with water instead!

items.label: text
items.text: Safety Note: Wear eye protection and avoid skin contact with the salts and their solutions.

items.label: text
items.text: In this experiment we have used excess zinc. Excess means more than enough zinc is present to ensure all the copper(ll) sulfate reacts. items.text: Z n ( s ) + C u S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) \rightarrow Z n S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) + C u ( s ) \quad \Delta H = - 2 1 5 k J / m o l

items.text: We have added the negative sign because we know that the temperature of the reaction mixture went up. The negative sign shows that this is an exothermic reaction; heat is released.

items.text: ACTIVITY 3

items.label: section_header
items.text: PRACTICAL: MEASURING ENTHALPY CHANGES WHEN SALTS DISSOLVE IN WATER

items.label: text
items.text: We can also use calorimetry experiments to work out the amount of heat given out/taken in when salts dissolve in water. The following procedure could be used:

items.label: list_item
items.text: Place a polystyrene cup in a 250 cm³ glass beaker.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Transfer 100 cm³ of water into the polystyrene cup using a measuring cylinder.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Record the initial temperature of the water.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Weigh 5.20g of ammonium chloride using a weighing boat on a balance.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Add the ammonium chloride to water and stir the solution vigorously until all the ammonium chloride has dissolved.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Record the minimum temperature.

items.label: text
items.text: The set-up is very similar to the one used in Activity 2, see Figure 19.12.
